transverse_findings.finding: The NQX Stage-B master independently reconciles 20010 Gate-A inputs to exactly 6570 survivorship instances and preserves the ten family receipt commits.
The recovery branch g30-stage-b-preflight-f03-f12-v191r1 still contains immutable Git source blobs for the family pipelines, parity implementations and recovery utilities.

F03 retains the exact Stage-B all-passers source control/recovery/qros_g30_f03_stage_b_all_passers_v191r1.py, Git blob SHA1 ee707a17a61fbf3b299c943e3ea515495f8021af. Its canonical stable_id and canonical JSONL serialization logic make exact row rematerialization testable against the original receipt hashes and roots.

Stage-B receipts preserve byte-identical Gate-A replay evidence, per-shard Stage-B output SHA256 values, decision roots/passer roots and primary-independent parity. These are cryptographic acceptance oracles; a rematerialized population is accepted only if every applicable oracle reconciles exactly.

Dropbox preserves prior-stage Campaign-30 artifacts including F12 Gate-A 24-shard authority, Gate-A passer replay and cluster membership artifacts. This disproves the earlier blanket assumption that all executable pre-Stage-B material was lost.

Dropbox contains /QROS/artifacts/faa75e645cf72e68447ed82ea5018d67ea1d8a6e373bbc24de6d8f0780d27cbb.tar.gz, size 70666933 bytes. Its contents have not yet been inspected through the available connector path and must not be assumed.

Several 40-hex identifiers previously treated as unresolved commit SHAs are Git blob SHA-1 object identities. Failure to resolve them with a commit endpoint was a type error, not evidence that the source bytes were absent.

NQX market authority is available independently of final-row recovery: canonical carrier SHA256 6da9cf67310c2c6689bd82c20882e5e8b652196147a458be58796e5103a22608, 559817687 records, 9516900679 bytes; 28/28 ZIP parts were physically available in the 2026-09-11 recovery runtime.

Forensic rematerialization is not a rerun of selection. Stage B remains scientifically closed. Membership is immutable and may only be materialized if the original cryptographic outputs/roots are reproduced exactly.

recovery_method.principle: Recreate missing bytes from preserved deterministic inputs/source lineage and accept only byte-identical or cryptographically equivalent outputs against frozen pre-existing oracles; never choose a new population.

acceptance_tiers.TIER_A_SOURCE_IDENTICAL: Exact historical source bytes plus exact inputs reproduce original output hashes, decision roots, passer roots and counts.
acceptance_tiers.TIER_B_CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY_EXECUTION_EQUIV: A recovery wrapper may differ from historical orchestration only if canonical outputs reproduce every preserved original hash/root/count exactly and independent parity remains exact. This tier proves the executable representation, not source identity of the wrapper.
acceptance_tiers.REJECT: Any mismatch in input identity, canonical row bytes, Stage-B shard SHA256, decision root, passer root, family count, BUY/SELL count, master root or independent parity.

forbidden: rerun Stage B as a new scientific selection
infer missing survivors from aggregate counts
accept approximate runner behavior without cryptographic reconciliation

population_unit.canonicality_rule: Parameter payload and stable_id must be serialized using the preserved family canonicalization. No regenerated row is authoritative until its family-level cryptographic oracle passes.

verified_source_objects.note: These Git blob identities prove immutable source objects exist. Except where explicitly proven (F03 all-passers Stage-B source), a transactional/source blob must not be equated with a receipt's historical local_stage_b_runner_sha256 until content hashing and role mapping reconcile.
